note: Movements that tend to load, or be limited by, each kind of injury. General guidance for planning, not clinical clearance. First matching rule wins. {S}/{s} is the injured side (Right/right) and {O}/{o} the opposite side. Edit freely. 'attack' and 'attack_sided' feed the Nice Scouting column: offensive actions a defender with this injury may have trouble guarding. They are the movements above turned around, general reasoning by this tracker and not checked against a study.

rules.name: Patellar tendon / patella
rules.basis: Van der Worp et al. 2014 (systematic review): horizontal landing after forward acceleration carries the greatest risk; stiff landing patterns linked to onset.
attack: Stop-and-go dribbles: sprint, hard stop, re-accelerate
Pump fakes to bait a jump, then drive
Offensive rebounds and putbacks (repeat jump contests)
Pace: push in transition so he has to sprint back and stop

rules.name: Achilles / calf / soleus
moves: Explosive toe-off when driving or cutting
sided: Push-off from the {s} leg when driving or cutting
rules.basis: General reasoning; Habets et al. 2017 (review) describes running and jumping as the activities held back until Achilles symptoms settle.
attack: Pump fakes and putbacks that force repeat jump attempts
Straight-line blow-bys and transition pace
Quick first step off a hesitation
Rim runs and lobs that need explosive toe-off
attack_sided: Drive to his {o} side so he has to push off the {s} leg to stay in front

rules.name: Hamstring
moves: Hard deceleration with a straight leg
Long strides and lunging forward (stretch under load)
rules.basis: Late-swing review (Scand J Med Sci Sports 2019): the most likely injury phase in high-speed running is late swing.
attack: Transition and early offense: make him run and recover at speed
Backdoor cuts and straight-line blow-bys
Stop-and-go dribbles (slow, then burst)
Rim runs that force long recovery strides

rules.name: Groin / adductor
moves: Quick cuts and crossovers in a wide stance
rules.basis: General sports-science reasoning by this tracker; not checked against a specific study.
attack: Crossovers and between-the-legs moves that force wide lateral slides
Side-step and step-back threes
Ball screens that make him slide, then recover laterally
Isolations that go both directions in a row

rules.name: Quadriceps / hip flexor
rules.basis: General sports-science reasoning by this tracker; not checked against a specific study.
attack: Hesitation and stop-and-go dribbles
Transition pace and rim runs
Pump fakes to bait a jump
First-step bursts out of triple threat

rules.name: Hip / glute
moves: Deep defensive stance and lateral slides
rules.basis: General sports-science reasoning by this tracker; not checked against a specific study.
attack: Hard drives that make him hold a low stance
Crossovers that force deep lateral slides
Post seals and bump-and-turn finishes in the lane
Quick cuts off screens

rules.name: Ankle
moves: Cutting and change of direction (sideways loads)
Landing from jumps, especially contested or uneven landings
rules.basis: General sports-science reasoning by this tracker; not checked against a specific study.
attack: Crossovers and hesitations that force sharp plants
Hard closeouts: shoot or drive off a late closeout
Pump fakes to draw him into awkward landings
Quick lateral screen-and-roll actions
attack_sided: Drive to his {o} side, or cross back toward his {s} side, so he plants on the {s} ankle

rules.name: Foot / toe
moves: Push-off in sprinting and jumping (forefoot loading)
sided: Push-off from the {s} foot when driving or cutting
rules.basis: General sports-science reasoning by this tracker; not checked against a specific study.
attack: Blow-bys in a straight line
Putbacks that force repeat jump takeoffs
Quick cuts and hard stops
Transition pace and long possessions
attack_sided: Drive to his {o} side so he pushes off the {s} foot to stay in front

rules.name: Knee
moves: Cutting and pivoting on a planted foot (twisting load)
rules.basis: General sports-science reasoning by this tracker; not checked against a specific study.
attack: Hesitation and crossovers that force planted cuts
Ball screens that switch him onto a quicker player
Stop-and-go dribbles (decelerate, then cut)
Pump fakes and putbacks that force repeat jumps
attack_sided: Drive to his {o} side, or cross back toward his {s} side, so he plants on the {s} leg

rules.name: Lower leg / shin
rules.basis: General sports-science reasoning by this tracker; not checked against a specific study.
attack: Transition pace and long possessions
Putbacks that force repeat jumps
Straight-line blow-bys

rules.name: Neck
rules.basis: General sports-science reasoning by this tracker; not checked against a specific study.
attack: Quick ball and player movement that needs fast head turns
Pump fakes he has to track with his head
Off-ball cuts behind his sightline

rules.name: Back / spine
moves: Boxing out and rebounding under load
rules.basis: General sports-science reasoning by this tracker; not checked against a specific study.
attack: Post seals and rim runs that need him to hold position
Fakes that make him rotate and recover
Offensive rebounds when he must box out under load

rules.name: Shoulder / arm
moves: Reaching to contest shots and passes
rules.basis: General sports-science reasoning by this tracker; not checked against a specific study.
attack: Shots and passes over his injured side
Quick passes through his reach
Drives that make him use that arm to contest

rules.name: Wrist / hand / finger
moves: Rebounding grip and strips (contact on the hand)
Contact when fouling or being fouled
rules.basis: General sports-science reasoning by this tracker; not checked against a specific study.
attack: Quick passes and strips he may not secure
Shots over his injured hand
Rebounds he has to grip and control

rules.name: Torso / core
rules.basis: General sports-science reasoning by this tracker; not checked against a specific study.
attack: Pump fakes and spins that make him rotate
Rim runs and transition pace
Offensive rebounds that need an explosive reach

rules.name: Head / face
moves: Contact near the head or face (rebounds, elbows, screens)
rules.basis: General sports-science reasoning by this tracker; not checked against a specific study.
attack: Fast ball movement and off-ball cuts that demand quick reads
Screening actions that need quick recovery
Pump fakes and shot fakes
